prompt: A vertical 9:16 photograph of a printed health-service advert poster, shot flat and square-on so the poster fills the entire frame edge to edge, matte paper with a fine print grain. The poster image is a candid-looking 35 mm photo of the man in the reference image sitting on a moulded plastic chair at a hospital bedside, leaning forward with his hands clasped solemnly between his knees, his head and shoulders large in the frame so his face takes up more than a third of the poster's height. Keep his face identical to the reference: about sixty, a long fleshy hooked nose with fine red veins, heavy-lidded narrow pale eyes, freckled blotchy ruddy skin, heavy jowls and a sly sideways half-smile. He wears a navy chalk-stripe suit. Behind him a pale green ward curtain and the edge of a white hospital blanket, softly out of focus. Light comes from a cool overhead fluorescent strip and a grey overcast window to his left, giving soft, slightly unflattering real-ward light. Across the top third of the poster, in huge heavy white block capitals on a deep charcoal band, the words SAVE OUR NHS, spelled exactly; these are the only words anywhere in the image. Natural hands with five fingers each. Thanks.
